# Smoke Test

Reads an interface definition and generates a minimal
smoke test that calls every method with valid input and
asserts no error and no panic. Provides baseline coverage
for new implementations before conformance suites are
wired.

## go:generate directive

```go
//go:generate testkit smoke -o smoke_store.gen_test.go Store
```

## Default output

`smoke_<name>.gen_test.go`

## What is generated

```go
// Code generated by testkit smoke. DO NOT EDIT.

package postgres_test

import (
    "context"
    "testing"

    "go.thesmos.sh/testkit"
    "example.com/myapp/store"
)

// SmokeStoreSpec provides the inputs for the Store
// smoke test. The developer provides a Factory and valid
// sample inputs — the smoke test calls every method once
// and asserts no error.
type SmokeStoreSpec struct {
    Factory  func() store.Store
    Entries  []store.Entry
}

func RunStoreSmoke(t *testing.T, spec SmokeStoreSpec) {
    t.Helper()
    ctx := testkit.TestContext(t)
    s := spec.Factory()

    t.Run("Put", func(t *testing.T) {
        err := s.Put(ctx, store.PutRequest{
            Entries: spec.Entries,
        })
        testkit.NoError(t, err, "Put smoke")
    })

    t.Run("Get", func(t *testing.T) {
        _, err := s.Get(ctx, "key")
        testkit.NoError(t, err, "Get smoke")
    })

    t.Run("Count", func(t *testing.T) {
        _, err := s.Count(ctx, store.CountRequest{})
        testkit.NoError(t, err, "Count smoke")
    })

    // ... one subtest per method
}
```

## Injection point

```go
// In the plugin's test file — hand-written:
func TestStore_Smoke(t *testing.T) {
    RunStoreSmoke(t, SmokeStoreSpec{
        Factory: func() store.Store { return setup(t) },
        Entries: []store.Entry{{Status: 1, Data: []byte("smoke")}},
    })
}
```

## Why

Conformance suites are comprehensive but require careful
wiring. Smoke tests are the "does it turn on?" check —
trivial to wire, fast to run, and catch the most basic
failures (nil pointer dereferences, missing initialization,
wrong SQL table names). They serve as a stepping stone:
wire smoke first, then conformance, then model.

## Scale

~40 interfaces x ~30 lines = ~1,200 lines.
